claims.text: VPEngine uses a shared foundation model backbone to extract image representations that are shared across specialized task heads running in parallel, reducing redundant feature-extraction computation.
claims.evidence_quote: Our framework architecture leverages a shared foundation model backbone that extracts image representations, which are efficiently shared, without any unnecessary GPU-CPU memory transfers, across multiple specialized task-specific model heads running in parallel. This design eliminates the computational redundancy inherent in feature extraction component when deploying traditional sequential models

claims.text: An example using DINOv2 with depth, object detection, and semantic segmentation heads achieves up to 3x speedup compared to sequential execution.
claims.evidence_quote: We demonstrate our framework's capabilities through an example implementation using DINOv2 as the foundation model with multiple task (depth, object detection and semantic segmentation) heads, achieving up to 3x speedup compared to sequential execution.

claims.text: Each task's inference frequency can be adjusted dynamically at runtime.
claims.evidence_quote: Building on CUDA Multi-Process Service (MPS), VPEngine offers efficient GPU utilization and maintains a constant memory footprint while allowing per-task inference frequencies to be adjusted dynamically during runtime.

claims.text: The example implementation demonstrates end-to-end real-time performance at at least 50 Hz on NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX for TensorRT-optimized models.
claims.evidence_quote: Our example implementation demonstrates end-to-end real-time performance at $\geq$50 Hz on NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX for TensorRT optimized models.

claims.text: VPEngine is designed to address redundant computation and memory use when deploying multiple perception models on robotic platforms.
claims.evidence_quote: Deploying multiple machine learning models on resource-constrained robotic platforms for different perception tasks often results in redundant computations, large memory footprints, and complex integration challenges. In response, this work presents Visual Perception Engine (VPEngine), a modular framework designed to enable efficient GPU usage for visual multitasking

claims.text: VPEngine uses a shared foundation-model backbone, such as DINOv2, to extract image representations that are reused by specialized depth, object-detection, and semantic-segmentation heads running in parallel.
claims.evidence_quote: Our framework architecture leverages a shared foundation model backbone that extracts image representations, which are efficiently shared, without any unnecessary GPU-CPU memory transfers, across multiple specialized task-specific model heads running in parallel. ... using DINOv2 as the foundation model with multiple task (depth, object detection and semantic segmentation) heads

claims.text: The extracted features are shared with task heads with zero-copy transfers and remain in GPU memory.
Sharing the backbone eliminates redundant feature-extraction computation compared with traditional sequential models.
claims.evidence_quote: This design eliminates the computational redundancy inherent in feature extraction component when deploying traditional sequential models

claims.text: Each task's inference frequency can be adjusted independently and dynamically at runtime.
claims.evidence_quote: VPEngine offers efficient GPU utilization and maintains a constant memory footprint while allowing per-task inference frequencies to be adjusted dynamically during runtime.

claims.text: For example, object detection could run at 50 Hz while semantic segmentation runs at 10 Hz.
The framework supports dynamic task prioritization based on application demands.
claims.evidence_quote: This design eliminates the computational redundancy inherent in feature extraction component when deploying traditional sequential models while enabling dynamic task prioritization based on application demands.

claims.text: Using CUDA MPS, VPEngine maintains a constant memory footprint.
claims.evidence_quote: Building on CUDA Multi-Process Service (MPS), VPEngine offers efficient GPU utilization and maintains a constant memory footprint

claims.text: The constant memory footprint is guaranteed regardless of how many tasks are active.
The example implementation achieved up to a 3x speedup over sequential execution.
claims.evidence_quote: We demonstrate our framework's capabilities through an example implementation using DINOv2 as the foundation model with multiple task (depth, object detection and semantic segmentation) heads, achieving up to 3x speedup compared to sequential execution.

claims.text: The example achieved end-to-end real-time performance at at least 50 Hz on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX using TensorRT-optimized models.
claims.evidence_quote: Our example implementation demonstrates end-to-end real-time performance at $\geq$50 Hz on NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX for TensorRT optimized models.

claims.text: VPEngine is open source and provides ROS2 C++ bindings for Humble.
claims.evidence_quote: The framework is written in Python and is open source with ROS2 C++ (Humble) bindings for ease of use by the robotics community across diverse robotic platforms.

claims.text: The approach in source [3] uses a mixture-of-experts vision architecture for multiple vision tasks.
claims.evidence_quote: We propose to modify and scale up mixture-of-experts (MoE) vision transformers, so that they can simultaneously learn classification, detection, and segmentation

claims.text: Sources [4] and [5] discuss efficient adaptation techniques involving adapters and few-shot learning, respectively.
claims.evidence_quote: Our work suggests that the use of adapters, strategically integrated into a pre-trained backbone model, can be successful in reducing both bandwidth and memory requirements for the target extraterrestrial device.

claims.text: Source [5] concerns few-shot semantic segmentation for robot grasping using foundation models.
claims.evidence_quote: We propose to overcome all these limitations by combining the impressive generalization capability reached by foundation models with a high-performing few-shot classifier

claims.text: Euclidean space is the de facto geometric setting for machine learning architectures, but this choice has fundamental limitations at large scale.
claims.evidence_quote: Euclidean space has been the de facto geometric setting for machine learning architectures. However, recent literature has demonstrated that this choice comes with fundamental limitations. At a large scale, real-world data often exhibits inherently non-Euclidean structures

claims.text: These structures are challenging to capture within Euclidean spaces.
claims.evidence_quote: It is challenging to effectively capture these structures within the constraints of Euclidean spaces.

claims.text: The paper argues that moving beyond Euclidean geometry is necessary to maintain the scaling law for next-generation foundation models, rather than merely being an optional enhancement.
claims.evidence_quote: This position paper argues that moving beyond Euclidean geometry is not merely an optional enhancement but a necessity to maintain the scaling law for the next-generation of foundation models.

claims.text: Non-Euclidean geometries could allow foundation models to leverage these structures more efficiently.
claims.evidence_quote: By adopting these geometries, foundation models could more efficiently leverage the aforementioned structures.

claims.text: Task-aware adaptability could dynamically reconfigure embeddings to match the geometry of downstream applications, improving efficiency and expressivity.
claims.evidence_quote: Task-aware adaptability that dynamically reconfigures embeddings to match the geometry of downstream applications could further enhance efficiency and expressivity.

claims.text: The position is supported by theoretical and empirical investigations of prevalent foundation models.
claims.evidence_quote: Our position is supported by a series of theoretical and empirical investigations of prevalent foundation models.

claims.text: The proposed integration strategies are fine-tuning existing models, training from scratch, and hybrid approaches.
claims.evidence_quote: we outline a roadmap for integrating non-Euclidean geometries into foundation models, including strategies for building geometric foundation models via fine-tuning, training from scratch, and hybrid approaches.

claims.text: RiemannGFM uses a structural vocabulary of trees and cycles, constructs a product bundle to incorporate diverse geometries, and stacks Riemannian layers that learn the vocabulary on a Riemannian manifold.
claims.evidence_quote: The key innovation is the discovery of a simple yet effective structural vocabulary of trees and cycles, and we explore its inherent connection to Riemannian geometry. Concretely, we first construct a novel product bundle to incorporate the diverse geometries of the vocabulary. Then, on this constructed space, we stack Riemannian layers where the structural vocabulary, regardless of specific graph, is learned in Riemannian manifold offering cross-domain transferability.

claims.text: RiemannGFM is intended to provide cross-domain transferability.
claims.evidence_quote: the structural vocabulary, regardless of specific graph, is learned in Riemannian manifold offering cross-domain transferability.

claims.text: The supplied source describing the roadmap does not provide implementation details, specific manifold choices, or quantitative results for those roadmap strategies.
claims.evidence_quote: Finally, we outline a roadmap for integrating non-Euclidean geometries into foundation models, including strategies for building geometric foundation models via fine-tuning, training from scratch, and hybrid approaches.

claims.text: Real-world data across languages, vision, and the natural sciences often has non-Euclidean structures, including multi-way relationships, hierarchies, symmetries, and non-isotropic scaling, which are challenging to capture in Euclidean spaces.
claims.evidence_quote: At a large scale, real-world data often exhibits inherently non-Euclidean structures, such as multi-way relationships, hierarchies, symmetries, and non-isotropic scaling, in a variety of domains, such as languages, vision, and the natural sciences. It is challenging to effectively capture these structures within the constraints of Euclidean spaces.

claims.text: The position paper argues that moving beyond Euclidean geometry is necessary to maintain the scaling law for next-generation foundation models, and that adopting non-Euclidean geometries could help models leverage these structures more efficiently.
claims.evidence_quote: This position paper argues that moving beyond Euclidean geometry is not merely an optional enhancement but a necessity to maintain the scaling law for the next-generation of foundation models. By adopting these geometries, foundation models could more efficiently leverage the aforementioned structures.

claims.text: Task-aware adaptability that dynamically reconfigures embeddings to match downstream geometry could further improve efficiency and expressivity.
claims.evidence_quote: Task-aware adaptability that dynamically reconfigures embeddings to match the geometry of downstream applications could further enhance efficiency and expressivity.

claims.text: Proposed integration strategies for geometric foundation models include fine-tuning, training from scratch, and hybrid approaches.
claims.evidence_quote: Finally, we outline a roadmap for integrating non-Euclidean geometries into foundation models, including strategies for building geometric foundation models via fine-tuning, training from scratch, and hybrid approaches.

claims.text: RiemannGFM uses a shared structural vocabulary of trees and cycles, constructs a product bundle to incorporate their diverse geometries, and stacks Riemannian layers to learn the vocabulary in a Riemannian manifold for cross-domain transferability.
claims.evidence_quote: The key innovation is the discovery of a simple yet effective structural vocabulary of trees and cycles, and we explore its inherent connection to Riemannian geometry. Herein, we present a universal pretraining model, RiemannGFM. Concretely, we first construct a novel product bundle to incorporate the diverse geometries of the vocabulary. Then, on this constructed space, we stack Riemannian layers where the structural vocabulary, regardless of specific graph, is learned in Riemannian manifold offering cross-domain transferability.

claims.text: Graphs are non-Euclidean structures; the source says graph neural networks often lack generalization, existing graph foundation-model efforts primarily focus on text-attributed graphs, and sequential graph descriptions can neglect structural complexity.
claims.evidence_quote: Graph neural networks excel at learning graph data, the omnipresent non-Euclidean structure, but often lack the generalization capacity. Hence, graph foundation model is drawing increasing attention, and recent efforts have been made to leverage Large Language Models. On the one hand, existing studies primarily focus on text-attributed graphs, while a wider range of real graphs do not contain fruitful textual attributes. On the other hand, the sequential graph description tailored for the Large Language Model neglects the structural complexity, which is a predominant characteristic of the graph.

claims.text: DEMR integrates extrinsic manifold embedding into deep networks and optimizes within the embedded Euclidean space rather than directly optimizing geodesic loss; the source reports evidence on SE(3), quotient manifolds, and Grassmann-manifold outputs in vision tasks.
claims.evidence_quote: DEMR incorporates extrinsic manifold embedding into deep neural networks, which helps generate manifold representations. The DEMR approach does not directly optimize the complex geodesic loss. Instead, it focuses on optimizing the computation graph within the embedded Euclidean space, allowing for adaptability to various architectural requirements. We provide empirical evidence supporting the proposed concept on two types of manifolds, $SE(3)$ and its associated quotient manifolds. [...] The experimental results show that DEMR effectively adapts to point cloud alignment, producing outputs in $ SE(3) $, as well as in illumination subspace learning with outputs on the Grassmann manifold.

claims.text: Manify provides tools for embeddings in products of non-Euclidean spaces, classification and regression with data in such spaces, and manifold-curvature estimation.
claims.evidence_quote: Leveraging manifold learning techniques, Manify provides tools for learning embeddings in (products of) non-Euclidean spaces, performing classification and regression with data that lives in such spaces, estimating the curvature of a manifold, and more.

claims.text: The AirfRANS/NeuralFoil study uses KHRONOS and compares it with an MLP, GNN, and PINN.
claims.evidence_quote: Using the AirfRANS dataset as a high-fidelity benchmark and NeuralFoil to generate low-fidelity counterparts, this work compares the performance of KHRONOS with three contemporary model architectures: a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a graph neural network (GNN), and a physics-informed neural network (PINN).

claims.text: The aerodynamic study blends sparse high-fidelity data with low-fidelity information and reports that KHRONOS needs orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters and trains and infers faster at comparable accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: In this work, we blend sparse high-fidelity (HF) data with low-fidelity (LF) information to predict aerodynamic fields under varying constraints in computational resources.

claims.text: KHRONOS constructs continuously differentiable target fields by hierarchically composing per-dimension kernel expansions, tensorizing them into modes, and superposing them.
claims.evidence_quote: KHRONOS constructs continuously differentiable target fields with a hierarchical composition of per-dimension kernel expansions, which are tensorized into modes and then superposed.

claims.text: On a canonical 2D Poisson benchmark, KHRONOS obtained L2-square errors from 5e-4 down to 6e-11 across 16 to 512 degrees of freedom.
claims.evidence_quote: We evaluate KHRONOS on a canonical 2D, Poisson equation benchmark: across 16 to 512 degrees of freedom (DoFs), it obtained L_2-square errors of 5e-4 down to 6e-11.

claims.text: At controlled parameter count, the paper reports a greater than 100-fold gain over Kolmogorov Arnold Networks.
claims.evidence_quote: This represents a greater than 100-fold gain over Kolmogorov Arnold Networks (which itself reports a 100 times improvement on MLPs/PINNs with 100 times fewer parameters) when controlling for the number of parameters.

claims.text: The paper reports a 1e6-fold L2-square error improvement over standard linear FEM at comparable degrees of freedom.
claims.evidence_quote: This also represents a 1e6-fold improvement in L_2-square error compared to standard linear FEM at comparable DoFs.

claims.text: The paper reports sub-millisecond full-field predictions and sub-microsecond per-sample latency for inverse problems.
claims.evidence_quote: Inference complexity is dominated by inner products, yielding sub-millisecond full-field predictions that scale to an arbitrary resolution. For inverse problems, KHRONOS facilitates rapid, iterative level set recovery in only a few forward evaluations, with sub-microsecond per sample latency.

claims.text: KHRONOS is built upon variational principles, interpolation theory, and tensor decomposition.
claims.evidence_quote: Unlike traditional approaches, KHRONOS is built upon variational principles, interpolation theory, and tensor decomposition.

claims.text: These ingredients provide a mathematical basis for heavy pruning compared with dense neural networks, supporting resource efficiency.
claims.evidence_quote: These elements provide a mathematical basis for heavy pruning compared to dense neural networks.

claims.text: The study blends sparse high-fidelity data with low-fidelity information, using AirfRANS as the high-fidelity benchmark and NeuralFoil for low-fidelity counterparts.
claims.evidence_quote: Using the AirfRANS dataset as a high-fidelity benchmark and NeuralFoil to generate low-fidelity counterparts

claims.evidence_quote: We consider varying levels of high-fidelity data availability (0%, 10%, and 30%) and increasingly complex geometry parameterizations.

claims.text: The comparison involves KHRONOS, an MLP, a GNN, and a PINN.
claims.evidence_quote: this work compares the performance of KHRONOS with three contemporary model architectures: a multilayer perceptron (MLP), a graph neural network (GNN), and a physics-informed neural network (PINN).

claims.text: All models eventually achieve comparable predictive accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: Results indicate that, whilst all models eventually achieve comparable predictive accuracy

claims.evidence_quote: KHRONOS consistently requires orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters and delivers much faster training and inference than contemporary dense neural networks at comparable accuracy.

claims.text: OpenChemIE extracts information from individual modalities, including text, tables, and figures, then integrates the results into a document-level list of reactions.
claims.evidence_quote: OpenChemIE approaches the problem in two steps: extracting relevant information from individual modalities and then integrating the results to obtain a final list of reactions.

claims.text: Specialized neural models handle specific chemistry information-extraction tasks, such as parsing molecules or reactions from text or figures.
claims.evidence_quote: For the first step, we employ specialized neural models that each address a specific task for chemistry information extraction, such as parsing molecules or reactions from text or figures.

claims.text: Prior work mostly investigated reaction extraction from single modalities.
claims.evidence_quote: Complete extraction requires combining information across text, tables, and figures, whereas prior work has mainly investigated extracting reactions from single modalities.

claims.text: The single-modality focus of prior work is the reason OpenChemIE uses a module-per-modality design to cover a whole document.
RxnScribe treats reaction diagram parsing as structured prediction using sequence generation, condensing a traditional multi-stage pipeline into an end-to-end model for diagrams of varying styles.
claims.evidence_quote: We formulate this structured prediction task with a sequence generation approach, which condenses the traditional pipeline into an end-to-end model. We train RxnScribe on a dataset of 1,378 diagrams and evaluate it with cross validation, achieving an 80.0% soft match F1 score, with significant improvements over previous models.

claims.text: OpenChemIE integrates module outputs using chemistry-informed algorithms, enabling extraction of fine-grained reaction data from reaction condition and substrate scope investigations.
claims.evidence_quote: We then integrate the information from these modules using chemistry-informed algorithms, allowing for the extraction of fine-grained reaction data from reaction condition and substrate scope investigations.

claims.text: OpenChemIE achieved an F1 score of 69.5% on an annotated dataset of reaction schemes with R-groups and 64.3% accuracy when compared directly against Reaxys.
claims.evidence_quote: We meticulously annotate a challenging dataset of reaction schemes with R-groups to evaluate our pipeline as a whole, achieving an F1 score of 69.5%. Additionally, the reaction extraction results of \ours attain an accuracy score of 64.3% when directly compared against the Reaxys chemical database.

claims.text: A cross-modality scientific information-extraction work notes that core information may be in text, tables, or across both, and that existing paper-focused datasets mostly target specific manuscript parts and single modalities.
claims.evidence_quote: Moreover, core information can be present in either text or tables or across both. To close this gap in data availability and enable cross-modality IE, while alleviating labeling costs, we propose a semi-supervised pipeline for annotating entities in text, as well as entities and relations in tables, in an iterative procedure.

claims.text: That work proposes a semi-supervised annotation pipeline and releases a benchmark, a large-scale corpus, and the pipeline.
claims.evidence_quote: Based on this pipeline, we release novel resources for the scientific community, including a high-quality benchmark, a large-scale corpus, and a semi-supervised annotation pipeline.

claims.text: Anaphora resolution is important for comprehensive information extraction and critical for extracting reactions in chemical patents; the source identifies five anaphoric relations and studies model performance in noisy and noise-free environments.
claims.evidence_quote: Anaphora resolution is an important component of comprehensive information extraction, and is critical for extracting reactions. In chemical patents, there are five anaphoric relations of interest: co-reference, transformed, reaction associated, work up, and contained. Our goal is to investigate how the performance of anaphora resolution models for reaction texts in chemical patents differs in a noise-free and noisy environment and to what extent we can improve the robustness against noise of the model.

claims.text: ChemRAG-Toolkit supports five retrieval algorithms and eight LLMs, and RAG yields an average relative improvement of 17.4% over direct inference.
claims.evidence_quote: In addition, we present ChemRAG-Toolkit, a modular and extensible RAG toolkit that supports five retrieval algorithms and eight LLMs. Using ChemRAG-Toolkit, we demonstrate that RAG yields a substantial performance gain -- achieving an average relative improvement of 17.4% over direct inference methods.

claims.text: Global geometry representations can address the limited geometric information available to nodes in standard GNN-based CFD methods.

claims.text: The proposed MMHCO-HAR method extracts features from RGB frames and event streams, then fuses them with multi-modal heat conduction blocks and an adaptive policy-routing fusion module for classification.

claims.text: The reported agreement applies to the particular HAMLET evaluation validated in its human study, not as a general guarantee.

claims.text: Automatic metrics can capture only specific aspects of text quality, vary in effectiveness by task and dataset, and show inconsistent correlations with human judgment; validation practices remain unstructured.
claims.evidence_quote: We identify several key challenges: metrics often capture only specific aspects of text quality, their effectiveness varies by task and dataset, validation practices remain unstructured, and correlations with human judgment are inconsistent.

claims.text: These limitations also persist for LLM-as-a-Judge and RAG evaluation.
claims.evidence_quote: Importantly, we find that these challenges persist in the most recent type of metric, LLM-as-a-Judge, as well as in the evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), an increasingly relevant task in academia and industry.

claims.text: LLM judges agree with experts mainly on questions the judges can answer correctly when they lack correct references, while expert-written references largely mitigate this issue.
claims.evidence_quote: While not provided with a correct reference, judges show high agreement with human experts only on questions the judges were able to correctly answer themselves. We demonstrate that providing the judges with expert-written references largely mitigates this issue, highlighting the limits of using LLM-as-a-Judge without any form of human verification.

claims.text: The attack injects a few malicious texts into a RAG knowledge database to induce an LLM to generate an attacker-chosen target answer for an attacker-chosen target question.

claims.text: The attack is formulated as an optimization problem whose solution is a set of malicious texts.

claims.text: The work provides two solutions depending on the attacker's background knowledge, namely black-box and white-box settings.

claims.text: PoisonedRAG achieved a 90% attack success rate when injecting five malicious texts for each target question into a knowledge database with millions of texts.
claims.evidence_quote: Our results show PoisonedRAG could achieve a 90% attack success rate when injecting five malicious texts for each target question into a knowledge database with millions of texts.

claims.text: The evaluated defenses were insufficient against PoisonedRAG, highlighting the need for new defenses.

claims.text: The second named method is QLLM.
claims.evidence_quote: surpassing Smoothquant and QLLM by over 12 points

claims.text: QLLM uses adaptive channel reassembly: it disassembles outlier activation channels into sub-channels, merges similar channels to preserve the original channel count, and adaptively selects the number of sub-channels.
claims.evidence_quote: QLLM introduces an adaptive channel reassembly technique that reallocates the magnitude of outliers to other channels, thereby mitigating their impact on the quantization range. This is achieved by channel disassembly and channel assembly, which first breaks down the outlier channels into several sub-channels to ensure a more balanced distribution of activation magnitudes. Then similar channels are merged to maintain the original channel number for efficiency. Additionally, an adaptive strategy is designed to autonomously determine the optimal number of sub-channels for channel disassembly.

claims.text: QLLM also uses a small low-rank tuning stage whose parameters can be fused into the frozen quantized weights.
claims.evidence_quote: we propose an efficient tuning method that only learns a small number of low-rank weights while freezing the pre-trained quantized model. After training, these low-rank parameters can be fused into the frozen weights without affecting inference.

claims.text: QLLM quantizes 4-bit LLaMA-2-70B within 10 hours on a single A100-80G GPU.
claims.evidence_quote: QLLM quantizes the 4-bit LLaMA-2-70B within 10 hours on a single A100-80G GPU

claims.evidence_quote: We perform a systematic evaluation of state-of-the-art LMs on three tasks: estimating percentiles, drawing samples, and calculating probabilities. We evaluate three ways to provide context to LMs 1) anchoring examples from within a distribution or family of distributions, 2) real-world context, 3) summary statistics on which to base a Normal approximation. Models can make inferences about distributions, and can be further aided by the incorporation of real-world context, example shots and simplified assumptions, even if these assumptions are incorrect or misspecified. To conduct this work, we developed a comprehensive benchmark distribution dataset with associated question-answer pairs that we have released publicly.
